## Failure shape

A command such as `psu --resume su-<uuid>` can spend about 30 seconds at `host-handoff-lookup` and then say the agent has no resumable session even though the agent row and native transcript still exist.

Two independent conditions produce that output:

- A launcher newer than the operator can call `/api/adv/sessions/resumable?agentId=…` against an older operator. The older response has `sessions` but no `exact` marker. Treating the missing marker as absence hides a row whose `coordOwnerId` is the requested, globally unique owner.
- During host-code adoption, the launcher already knows `PAPERCUSP_SID`, but a parent-PID lookup scans every entry in `~/.papercusp/psu-pty`. That directory also contains sockets, event logs, and discovery records; its size grows with session history.

## Recovery rule

The launcher may accept a legacy response only when a returned resumable row has the exact requested `coordOwnerId` and an agent identity. A response with an explicit `exact` field still uses the stricter id/owner checks. This preserves identity binding while tolerating a lagging operator build.

When the adoption owner is known, read `<owner>.handoff.json` directly and retain the parent-PID check. Use the directory scan only when no owner is available. A parent mismatch is consumed and refused.

The regression tests live beside the launcher and PTY host: `apps/operator/lib/psu-launcher.test.ts`, `apps/operator/lib/psu-pty-host.test.ts`, and `apps/operator/lib/psu-adopt-first-turn.test.ts`.
